Definition: properly, accumulated; i.e. (by implication) a summit
BiblicalUsage: Men come down by the middle of the land, by the way of the plain of Meonenim, the watchers tell Abimelech. And Gog's people will take a spoil from those who dwell in the midst of the land. The word is the centre, the midst, the navel, the highest part: the middle of things, where the eye rests and the enemy aims.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the middle of the land is where the Bible's battles are fought: not at the edges, but at the heart of it, and God sees the centre better than any watcher.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
